selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: usb-storage module not loaded before change
selected_evidence.summary: lsmod grep returned 0 matches for usb_storage prior to any modification; modinfo confirmed module exists on disk
Created /etc/modprobe.d/usb-storage-blacklist.conf with blacklist + install /bin/true directives; modprobe usb-storage then exits 0 but lsmod count remains 0, proving the module cannot be loaded
Rebuilt initramfs with dracut -f; lsinitrd confirms /etc/modprobe.d/usb-storage-blacklist.conf with both directives is embedded in the boot image used at next boot
Captured boot_id bdbfa15c-cfc4-4b36-8edd-d0a49076e9c5 and uptime -s (2026-08-26 10:33:30) as the pre-restart boot identity baseline
Issued 'sudo shutdown -r now' backgrounded with nohup; command returned exit 0 with PID before the connection dropped

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proof via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Immediately after reboot issued, exec timed out (node down); on next poll exec succeeded with new boot_id 3ad85187-982b-4653-8397-d9813ff8183c and new uptime -s (2026-09-04 23:27:45), proving an actual restart occurred, not just a service bounce
After reboot, lsmod shows usb_storage count 0, modprobe usb-storage still exits 0 without loading it (via install /bin/true), and the blacklist config file is intact on the running filesystem
